- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5% of spike magnitude.  
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply 0.5–1.5% upward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to mean-revert; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.  
- When sentiment is stable (mostly 0.00 or 0.67), model overfits recent trends; use 3-day moving average to dampen forecast.
